gen-righteous-gf-radio-canada: Righteous is commanding and fun, each letter like a thin steel rod bent into shape, with rounded forms packed full. Righteous grabs attention; Radio Canada sans keeps its lowercase tall and clear.
gen-righteous-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro is a sans-serif with broad gaps at its terminals and a tiny step between lowercase and caps. And under Righteous, its steady weight would carry a page of text smoothly from word to word.
gen-righteous-gf-ruda: Every Righteous letter looks like a thin steel rod bent into shape. Ruda, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed rounds and a sizable x-height, gives that loud heading something friendly to hand off to.
gen-righteous-gf-saira: Righteous draws its letters like twine pressed into a flat surface, commanding and a bit playful. Saira, a sans whose s shapes are see-through and whose rounds reach high, keeps text crisp line after line.
gen-righteous-gf-sen: Fun and commanding, Righteous looks like thin steel rod bent into every letter, with rounded forms packed tight. Sen traces each letter at constant weight, which carries long reading smoothly.
gen-righteous-gf-stack-sans-headline: Stack Sans Headline reads crisp and approachable, with wide gaps. Made small, Righteous loses some of its command, though the sans-serif's deep middle band stays easy to take in.
gen-silkscreen-fs-asap: Silkscreen leaves breathing space around every letter, like spaghetti laid out. Asap, a sans-serif whose body height nearly matches its capitals, gives the retro heading a sturdy, readable partner.
gen-silkscreen-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen spaces its letters out like spaghetti. Shrunk down, Silkscreen loses its charm, whereas Be Vietnam Pro keeps a high mean line and curve endings that never touch.
gen-silkscreen-general-sans: Clean from first letter to last, General Sans keeps steady pen pressure and a tall x-height. And Silkscreen, with spaghetti-like lines, belongs big and short, where its lo-fi spacing shows.
gen-silkscreen-manrope: Silkscreen wraps every letter in space you can almost feel, its line drawn like spaghetti with a retro, lo-fi hum. It works big and brief; Manrope handles the rest, bright and friendly.
